PHOTO TILE (Lantern 1.24.42) -- AN INDEPENDENT REVIEW BY A PERSON'S USE
=======================================================================
Reviewer: a separate agent that did not write the tile. Date: 2026-11-26.
Build tested: the frozen build photo_r1/index.html (its PHOTO_* and GUIDE_PHOTO modules are byte-for-byte those of
src/lantern.inner.html on branch lantern-1.24.42, commit 68b87e2). Chromium (Playwright), headless, 1400 x 900
unless said; also 1366 x 768 and 390 x 844.

Files here
  make_inputs.py   makes inputs/ (a camera-like JPEG with EXIF, the same with EXIF orientation 6, a logo with
                   soft transparency, a grey scan, a screenshot, 1x1, 6000x40, 40x6000, a horizon tilted 5 deg,
                   a slanted document, three shots with a walker, a red-eye face, a layered PSD by psd-tools,
                   three small batch files). 432 KB in all. The 12 MP photo is made at run time.
  harness.py       the server, Chromium, and a person's actions (menus by click, tools by click, drags, keys,
                   typing into boxes, the Layers panel). State is only READ, to check results.
  run_review.py    every check. python3 run_review.py [build.html] [section ...]
                   sections: sel move paint retouch make crop transform menus history layers files actions keys
                   robust phone. Prints PASS/FAIL per check and "N checks, M failed". A full run takes ~25 min.
  cases.json       the run as found: 274 checks, 38 failed (every check, PASS or FAIL, with what was seen).
                   One full run, plus two type-layer checks added after it and run on the same build.
  evidence/        screenshots: the 1366x768 tool column cut off, the phone menu off the right edge, others.

HOW SURE: "certain" = reproduced in the browser and traced to the code; "high" = reproduced, Photoshop's behaviour
well known; "medium" = reproduced, but Photoshop's exact behaviour is from memory and could differ in some version.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------
THE MOST IMPORTANT FINDINGS FIRST
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

1. Dropping a picture onto an open picture is not caught: the browser opens the file instead, and the work is lost.
   Steps: open any picture, paint a stroke, drag another picture file from the desktop onto the picture.
   What happens: nothing in the tile (or Lantern) cancels 'dragover' or 'drop' outside the start screen's dashed box
   (check "Drop a picture on an open picture": defaultPrevented false for both). In Chrome and Edge an uncancelled
   drop of a file navigates the tab to that file: Lantern is replaced by the picture, the unsaved edit is gone.
   The same happens on the start screen if the file is dropped anywhere but inside the dashed box.
   Should: the help says "drop or paste a picture"; Photoshop places a file dropped on an open document as a new
   layer (File > Place Embedded). At least the page must cancel dragover/drop everywhere in the tile.
   Sure: high (the event part is certain; the navigation is the browser's documented default and could not be
   watched in headless Playwright).

2. The start screen's "New..." button does nothing and throws an error.
   Steps: open the Photo tile with no picture; click "New...". (Ctrl+N there does nothing either.)
   What happens: page error "Cannot read properties of null (reading 'w')" -- P.dialog reads api.d.w and the
   dialog host (S.dlg) only exists once a picture is open. No box appears.
   Should: the New box (size, resolution, background), as File > New does once a picture is open.
   A person with no photo cannot start a blank picture. Sure: certain.

3. A box (Levels, Hue/Saturation, any filter) is not modal: what it previews gets baked into the next thing done
   on the picture, and Cancel can no longer take it away.
   Steps: Image > Adjustments > Hue/Saturation, move Hue (the sky turns purple in the preview); without closing the
   box, pick the Brush and paint a stroke on the picture; then press Cancel in the box.
   What happens: the sky stays purple ([157,95,226] where it was [95,151,226]); History shows one step "Brush"
   and no Hue/Saturation step -- the previewed change was folded into the brush stroke (the stroke ends the open
   preview state with D.end). Undo of "Brush" is the only way back.
   Should: Photoshop's adjustment and filter boxes are modal (the picture cannot be painted while one is open);
   Cancel "leaves the picture as it was" (the tile's own PHOTO_DIALOGS comment). Sure: certain.

4. Renaming a layer by double-clicking its name never works, and the letters typed then go to the tool keys.
   Steps: in the Layers panel double-click a layer's name; type "Sky paint"; Enter.
   What happens: no text box appears (the first click rebuilds the whole list with innerHTML = "", so the second
   click lands on a new element and no dblclick event is ever fired -- counted 0 dblclick events). The typed
   letters switch tools (the "t" of "paint" chose the Type tool, "p", "a", "i" ...).
   Should: the help: "double-click its name to rename it"; Photoshop opens the name for editing.
   (Double-clicking an adjustment layer's picture does work: those thumbnails are cached, the names are not.)
   Sure: certain.

5. Backspace or Delete with nothing selected wipes the whole layer to see-through -- also while placing the
   corners of a Polygonal Lasso.
   Steps: (a) open a photo, press Delete (or Backspace). (b) Polygonal Lasso: click three corners, press Backspace
   to take back the last one, as in Photoshop.
   What happens: Edit > Clear runs on the whole layer: the photo becomes fully transparent (History "Clear"). In
   (b) the corners stay and the layer is wiped; the polygon is not shortened.
   Should: Photoshop's Polygonal Lasso: Backspace/Delete removes the last corner, Esc cancels the polygon. Photoshop
   does not empty a whole layer from Delete with no selection (on a Background layer it offers the Fill box).
   Ctrl+Z does restore it, but a person who does not notice saves an empty picture. Sure: high.

6. After clicking any checkbox, slider or list on the options bar or in the Layers panel, the keys stop working
   until the picture is clicked.
   Steps: tick "Lock" in the Layers panel (or move a slider, or choose a blend mode), then press ] or B or D or
   Ctrl+Z. Also: type a Size on the options bar and press Enter, then press E.
   What happens: nothing -- PHOTO_TILE's keydown treats every INPUT and SELECT as typing (checkboxes and range
   sliders included) and returns; focus stays there after Enter.
   Should: in Photoshop the tool keys and [ ] keep working after a panel checkbox; Enter in an options-bar field
   commits and gives the keys back to the picture. Only text and number fields being typed in should hold keys.
   Sure: certain (the behaviour); high (Photoshop).

6b. A tool letter pressed in the middle of a brush stroke leaves the stroke half-made; the next box cancelled
   then erases it.
   Steps: Brush, press the mouse and paint; while still holding the button press M (or any tool letter); let go.
   Then Image > Adjustments > Levels... and Cancel.
   What happens: the red stroke shows, but no History step is made and the document stays "open" (d.open true:
   the Brush's up() is never called because the tool in hand changed). Cancelling the Levels box (D.cancel)
   then silently wipes the stroke; Ctrl+Z cannot bring it back.
   Should: the stroke ends as one "Brush" step when the button is let go, whatever key was pressed. In Photoshop a
   tool key during a stroke does not lose the stroke. Sure: certain.

7. On a 1366 x 768 laptop window the tool column is cut off: Crop, Perspective Crop, Type, Shape, both colour
   swatches, Swap, Default colours and Quick Mask are below the bottom edge (swatch top at 848 px, column ends at
   754 px), with no visible scroll bar. evidence/laptop_1366x768_tools_cut_off.jpg.
   Should: every tool and the colours visible, as Photoshop's toolbar (two columns, or a smaller layout).
   1366 x 768 is the commonest laptop screen. Sure: certain.

8. Ctrl+Z also changes which layer is chosen, so the next command changes a layer the person did not choose.
   Steps: Layer via Copy (the copy is chosen), Deselect, click the Background in the Layers panel, Image >
   Adjustments > Invert, Ctrl+Z, Invert again.
   What happens: after Ctrl+Z the copy layer is chosen again, and the second Invert inverts the copy, not the
   Background the person picked. The tile's own Cancel keeps the chosen layer ("choosing a layer is not a step
   of its own", PHOTO_DOC) but Undo does not.
   Sure: certain (the behaviour); medium that Photoshop never does this (Photoshop's History states do carry the
   target layer in some cases), but the tile is inconsistent with its own rule.

9. Editing words already on the picture applies the options bar's current size and colour to them.
   Steps: Type tool, size 40, blue, click and type "Hello", choose Move. Then pick red and size 12 on the bar,
   Type tool, click the words, add "!", click away.
   What happens: the layer becomes "Hello!" at size 12 and red (font, bold, italic, alignment, tracking too:
   finishType builds the spec from the bar and d.fg).
   Should: Photoshop loads the type layer's own settings into the options bar when it is edited and keeps them;
   the bar's values change the words only when chosen while the words are selected. Sure: certain.

10. After moving words with the Move tool, clicking them with the Type tool starts new empty words instead of
    editing them (the hit test uses the text's original x/y, not where the layer now is).
    Steps: make "Hello!", Move it 100 px right and down, Type tool, click on it. A new empty box opens there.
    Sure: certain.

11. Type layers are made into pixels silently.
    (a) Free Transform (Ctrl+T, drag a corner, Enter) on a type layer turns it into a pixel layer; the status line
        still says "Free Transform: Enter applies, Esc leaves it". Photoshop scales and turns type and keeps it
        editable.
    (b) Image > Adjustments (e.g. Invert) on a type layer makes it pixels with no message at that time; the note
        is only shown at the next Save -- and a note is also queued by a box's PREVIEW, so after Gaussian Blur's
        box is Cancelled (the layer still words) Ctrl+S says "Saved photo.psd -- "Sky" was made into pixels".
        PHOTO_OPS says "the tile says so"; Photoshop asks first.
    Sure: certain.

12. Free Transform: choosing another tool part-way drops the transform without a word.
    Steps: Ctrl+T, drag the layer 100 px, click the Brush. The layer is back where it was, no History step.
    Should: Photoshop asks "Apply the transformation?" (Apply / Cancel / Don't Apply). Sure: high.

13. Free Transform: the W %, H % and Angle boxes keep the last values typed. After one transform with W 50, the
    next Ctrl+T shows W 50 while the box is at 100%; typing an angle then also halves the width.
    Should: each Free Transform starts at 100%, 100%, 0 deg. Sure: certain.

14. Quick Mask with nothing selected starts with NOTHING selected (the whole picture red); Photoshop starts with
    everything selected (no red), so black paint takes the stroke away. Here black paint does nothing and Q
    again selects all. The help ("paint the selection itself, white in, black out") then works only half.
    Sure: high.

15. Keys the menus show that do not work:
    - Export As shows Ctrl+Shift+Alt+W; pressing it does nothing (the key matcher builds "Ctrl+Alt+Shift+W" and
      compares strings). Certain.
    - Ctrl+T (Free Transform), Ctrl+N (New) and Ctrl+Shift+N (New Layer) are taken by Chrome and Edge (new tab,
      new window, private window) before any page sees them; they cannot work in a browser tab. Not testable in
      Playwright (it delivers keys to the page directly); from Chromium's documented reserved keys. High.
    - Alt+Backspace / Ctrl+Backspace (fill with foreground / background), among Photoshop's most used keys,
      do nothing. High.
    - Esc does not close an open menu. Certain.

16. History Brush after more than 50 steps paints from a later state, not the picture as opened.
    Steps: open a photo, Invert, nudge with the arrow keys 52 times, History Brush over the photo.
    What happens: it paints the inverted picture back (History keeps 50 states and drops the oldest; the
    brush's source is an index into that list, and the tile keeps no "as opened" snapshot).
    Should: Photoshop's History Brush paints from the opening snapshot, which is kept however many steps follow;
    the help says "paints back the picture as it was opened". Sure: certain.

17. History panel: the undone steps are listed greyed but cannot be clicked to go forward again (only Ctrl+Shift+Z
    brings them). Photoshop lets a click on a later (greyed) state go to it. Sure: certain / high.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------
SMALLER FINDINGS
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
18. Marquee: Shift+Alt held before dragging (intersect, as the help says) also makes the shape a centred square,
    so the overlap is wrong (got the first rectangle back unchanged). Photoshop: Shift+Alt before the drag only
    intersects. Certain.
19. Polygonal Lasso: Esc does not cancel the corners placed so far (they stay, and the next click continues the
    polygon). Photoshop: Esc cancels. Certain.
20. Crop with a ratio (1:1), dragged up and to the left: the box does not keep its corner where the drag began
    (b.y is taken from the pointer but the height from the width), so a different area is cropped. Certain.
21. Pencil is soft-edged at sizes above 2 px (alpha values 24, 162, 234 ... along a 6 px line). Photoshop's
    Pencil is always hard-edged. Certain.
22. Move with a selection on the Background (and the Eraser on it) leaves see-through pixels; Photoshop fills the
    Background's hole with the background colour (the Background cannot be see-through). The tile has no
    special Background layer; a JPEG export then shows white there. Medium (a design choice to note).
23. Image > Image Rotation > Straighten by the Ruler line: the horizon comes out level (pass), but the corners are
    left see-through; Photoshop's Ruler "Straighten Layer" crops them away, and Arbitrary rotation fills the
    Background's corners with the background colour. Medium.
24. A phone (390 x 844): the Filter menu runs past the right edge (menu right at 415 px), the page scrolls sideways
    while it is open, and the shortcut column is cut. evidence/phone_menu.png. Everything else checked was
    reachable. Certain.
25. History names are not the menu's names: "Hue Sat", "Gaussian", "Box", "Motion", "Radial", "Surface",
    "Unsharp", "Dust", "Brightness", "Polar", "Halftone", "Lens" (Photoshop: "Hue/Saturation", "Gaussian Blur",
    "Unsharp Mask", "Dust & Scratches", "Brightness/Contrast" ...). Actions list them the same way. Certain.
26. Layers panel "Adjust..." then Cancel in its box leaves the new adjustment layer (and its History step) behind.
    A box with a Cancel button should leave nothing. Certain.
27. Layer mask from a selection keeps the selection active; Photoshop drops it. Because it stays, the next
    adjustment layer silently gets a mask from it (seen in this review). Medium-high.
28. Quick Selection: the first stroke adds to a marquee selection made before; Photoshop's first stroke starts a
    new selection ("New selection" mode, then "Add to"). Medium.
29. A tool letter pressed twice moves to the next tool of its group (B, B -> Pencil). Photoshop's default is that
    only Shift+letter cycles (Preferences > Use Shift Key for Tool Switch). The tile's help says so itself, so
    this is a difference, not a contradiction. High.
30. The first new layer is "Layer 2" (Photoshop: "Layer 1"). Trivial.
31. Esc in the middle of a marquee drag does not drop it (the selection is made on release). I am not sure
    Photoshop drops it either: listed as a FAIL in cases.json but low confidence, low importance.
32. Cosmetic: the collapsed Histogram panel's heading reads "Histogram" with "LuminosityRedGreenBlue" under it
    (the select's option texts copied into the summary). Invert is listed as "Invert..." though it opens no box.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------
WHAT WORKED (PASS in cases.json)
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
- Marquee/ellipse drag, Shift and Alt during the drag, Shift (add) and Alt (subtract) before it, the options bar's
  modes, Feather; Lasso; Polygonal Lasso closing on its first corner and by double-click; Magic Wand and its
  Tolerance; Quick Selection; Inverse, Reselect, Modify (Expand, Contract, Border, Feather), Color Range.
- Move (drag, arrows, Shift+arrows, with a selection, Auto-select); Layer via Copy/Cut with a soft selection.
- Brush size/hardness, Opacity vs Flow (a stroke crossing itself stays at 50% opacity; flow builds), Shift+click
  line, Alt+click pick, painting inside a selection, Lock transparency, masks (paint, Shift+click off), Eraser,
  Quick Mask painting white, D and X.
- Clone Stamp, Healing Brush, Spot Healing Brush, Patch (the wire across the sky taken out by each), Red Eye,
  Dodge, Burn, Sponge, Blur, Smudge.
- Paint Bucket; Gradient: linear, radial, angle, reflected, diamond, Shift to 45 deg; Type: point, paragraph that
  wraps, Esc, keys typed into the box stay there; Shape: every kind.
- Crop: box, side handle, Esc, 1:1, turning outside the box levels a tilted horizon; Perspective Crop; Eyedropper
  with Alt; Ruler angle and Straighten level; Zoom, Hand, Space-drag.
- Free Transform: move, corner keeps proportions, Shift frees, side handle, turn, Ctrl+corner distort, Esc exact,
  W % typed.
- All 54 adjustments and filters from the menus, on the Background with a layer above: with Preview on, OK gives
  exactly what was previewed; Cancel leaves every layer exactly as it was with no History step; only the chosen
  layer changes; Ctrl+Z gives back the exact pixels. Fade, Last Filter (Ctrl+Alt+F).
- Undo and redo exact for: crop, Image Size, Canvas Size, rotate 90, arbitrary rotation, flip, flatten, merge,
  mask from selection, Free Transform, adjustment layer, Stamp Visible.
- Layers: new, duplicate, delete, up/down, eye, Multiply, opacity, Clip, mask apply/delete, adjustment layers
  (made, changed by double-click, undone), Drop Shadow (live when moved), Stamp/Merge Down/Merge Visible/Flatten
  with the picture unchanged, Place, Stack Mode Median (the walker gone).
- Files: drop on the start screen's box, paste as a layer, EXIF orientation 6 upright, grey PNG, a psd-tools PSD
  with hidden and Multiply layers; File Info with the camera's details; Ctrl+S .psd read back by psd-tools (every
  layer, Screen mode, mask, its picture equal to the tile's within 3 levels) and by ImageMagick; Export As each of
  psd, png, jpg, webp, gif, tif, bmp, pdf opened by PIL/psd-tools/poppler at the right size, JPEG without the
  camera's details, JPEG quality makes a difference; Print; Open as PDF in the PDF tile.
- Actions: record two menu commands, play them on another picture (identical), delete; Batch of three files
  through "Black and white" to JPEG: a zip of three grey JPEGs at their own sizes.
- Keys: every tool letter, Shift+letter cycling, zoom keys, grid, Ctrl+A, Ctrl+C/V, Ctrl+L/M/U/B, Ctrl+Alt+Shift+B,
  Ctrl+Alt+I/C, Shift+F5, Ctrl+Shift+R, Ctrl+Alt+Shift+I; keys typed inside a box stay in it; Esc/Enter in a box.
- Robustness: a 12 MP JPEG (4000 x 3000) opened in 0.5 s; a long brush stroke 3.6 s; Gaussian Blur 5 with its
  preview and OK 10.7 s, OK equal to the preview; two undos 0.6 s; Image Size kept proportions. 1 x 1 (brush,
  crop, blur, Image Size to 64), 6000 x 40 and 40 x 6000 (fit, rotate), a logo's transparency (Magic Wand),
  20 quick clicks = 20 steps and 20 quick undos, leaving the tile and coming back (picture, layers, History and
  keys all still there).
- Phone 390 x 844: no sideways scroll on opening, every button within the width, the Levels box fits and its OK
  can be pressed, the picture and the swatches are there (but see finding 24).
- No uncaught page errors except the start screen's New... (finding 2).

-----------------------------------------------------------------------
WHAT I COULD NOT TEST
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
- A real drag of a file from the desktop (only that the page does not cancel the drop; finding 1).
- The browser's reserved keys (Ctrl+T, Ctrl+N, Ctrl+Shift+N) in a real Chrome window; a Mac's Cmd and Option keys
  (Option+letter gives other characters in e.key, which the key matcher may not read).
- The real system clipboard from another program (navigator.clipboard.read needs a permission prompt); the paste
  was tested with a paste event carrying a file.
- A pen's pressure, two-finger pinch on a real touch screen, the printed paper.
- How results look to a person (Adam's to judge): only numbers were compared, apart from the screenshots.
- Photoshop itself was not run here: its behaviour is cited from Adobe's documentation as I know it; where I am
  less sure it says "medium".
